readings.source_reading: A leftward arrow, with the head at about x≈160 and a shaft running to about x≈435, at about y≈3345. The shaft has a small gap near the gutter, at about x≈330–345. The arrowhead and most of the shaft lie left of the target leaf's gutter edge (about x≈340–370), on the visible strip of the facing leaf. Only the short right-hand segment lies on fol. 79. A separate facing-page trace, '[?]tsā ca ←', at x≈0–280, y≈2390–2440, is the tail of the fol. 78b note ending 'cikitsā ca'. The dash b901 (x≈400–515) lies on the target leaf.
readings.evidence: In native tiles [0,3216] and [0,1608], the gutter fold is at x≈330–370. The 78b native tile shows the matching note text and its arrows at the same levels.

readings.source_reading: 'ff.10-72 (m.34) (inc[plt?])'. The parenthetical is a cramped abbreviation, roughly 'incplt', and is not written out as 'incomplete'. Above the shelfmark is a small figure, possibly '2', struck with a horizontal stroke: ⟦[2?]⟧. The extent reads '6' followed by a struck digit with '2' above it: 6⟦[illegible]⟧. The struck digit may be '1' or '4', but this is not legible enough to decide.

The line reads '✓⟦c?⟧d. 262(4) ——— Ɔ.C° Gūḍhārthaprakāśikā [struck mark] 1780 : 4 : 13/14 ⟦1[?]⟧ : D'. The siglum is a reversed C followed by a point, then a heavily inked C with a superscript small circle. The next line has 'ff.1-3(3bis), S. 1837.' in the shelfmark column, with 'L, x, 4097' above '°⟦khaṇḍana⟧, by Bālakṛṣṇa Pāyaguṇḍe' (written 'Payagunde' with dots). There is no other shelfmark between these lines and the next cross-reference (Citsukhamuni), so attachment to d.262(4) is probable but not explicitly marked.

A wavy line cancels 'd. 62 (9)ᶜ City Upaniṣ[att?]'. 'See' is written above, just before '(= Taittirīya Āraṇyaka III).', and the parenthesis does not appear struck. The figures 'n.d.: 10: 10' are struck, and ': D' is apparently left. The ditto dashes of d.932(9), d.932(1) and d.60(3) follow. '4.' and '2' are written above the latter two dashes. The text does not determine which title the dittos now refer to after the cancellation.
